## 分诊 · `domain:cli` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** The repair is in `packages/cli/test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts` ⇒ `domain:cli`. Confirmed on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-05T00:16:44Z): `probeOriginCheck` is defined at `:305` and called at `:485`, `:495`, **`:505`** — and `:505` is the `NODE_ENV=test` case named in the failure. The stack's `:426` / `:505` frames line up with the file as it stands.

### Grade — p2

- **Not p3.** ⭐ The cost is not "a test failed" — it is that **a flake in a required shard evicts a merge-queue entry**, which costs *every* lane a queue cycle (~25 min), and under the one-re-run rule **a second unlucky roll converts a flake into a "real" red.** That is a systemic tax on throughput, not a local annoyance, and it landed on a PR (#15506) whose diff was two `scripts/` gates the CLI does not import.
- **Not p1**: nothing ships wrong, and the product behaviour under test (`#11113`, `NODE_ENV` defaulting to production) is not implicated.

⭐ **The attribution is properly controlled**, which is what makes this actionable rather than a shrug: `packages/cli` was **1 failed / 2880 passed / 6 expected-fail**, and **every other merge-group run in the same window** (#15507, #15492, #15516, #15517, #15512) **passed the same shard.** ⇒ Not a broken shard, not a broken tree — one test.

And the diagnosis is a reading, not a guess: `probeOriginCheck` `fetch`es a spawned `os serve`, and `UND_ERR_SOCKET` / *other side closed* with **`bytesRead: 0`** means the server closed the socket **before answering**. ⇒ a readiness/lifecycle race in the harness, ⛔ not an assertion about the production default.

### Boundary test — Tests only, no manual floor

The fix changes no product code. Ordinary lane work.

### ⛔ The one fence that matters, and it is absolute

> The repair belongs to whoever owns the e2e's readiness probe (**wait for the server's own ready signal** / **retry the probe on `UND_ERR_SOCKET` a bounded number of times, with the reason stated**), **never to skipping or quarantining the test.**

Adopted verbatim and binding. ⛔ No `.skip`, no `.todo`, no quarantine list, no bumping a timeout and calling it fixed. This repo's rules already forbid it, and this card is the case where it would be most tempting because the test is slow (**shard duration 783 s**) and its subject is unglamorous.

⚠️ **Prefer the ready-signal over the retry.** A bounded retry on `UND_ERR_SOCKET` hides the race rather than removing it, and if the server is closing sockets for a *reason* other than not-yet-ready, a retry would mask a real defect. ⇒ If the retry is used, it must be **in addition to** waiting for the ready signal, and the "with the reason stated" clause is not optional — the comment must say which failure mode it absorbs and why that mode is benign.

⚠️ Also worth checking in the same pass: `probeOriginCheck` is called **three times** in this file (`:485`, `:495`, `:505`). Only `:505` was observed failing, but all three share the same probe. ⇒ Fix the helper, ⛔ not the one call site — otherwise this returns from a different line and reads as a new flake.

### Dedup — the card's own gap, carried forward

⚠️ REST `/search/issues` is 403 on that seat and MCP search was rate-limited at filing time, so the dedup was a **title-keyword pass over the open-issue list**, and the filer says plainly that *an older one may exist beyond that read.* ⛔ That is not a controlled zero. ⇒ Whoever picks this up should re-run a dedup search for this test file name; a prior flake card would carry earlier occurrences and turn "one eviction" into a rate.

⭐ Recorded for the record: reporting a merge-queue eviction as a **card with the run id, the queue head, the shard counts and the same-window controls** — rather than re-running and moving on — is what makes a flake measurable at all. This one has everything a fixer needs.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

## Dispatched — `domain:cli` execution seat (#6024)

Session `session_01D47qPfEWVPmhguWgBZCi5N`. Branch prefix `claude/issue-15545-*`. Claiming the card for this seat; the implementing agent will post its own claim before its first edit.

### Serial check — measured, not declared

The surface is `packages/cli/test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts`. Against the **complete** open-PR population (30 PRs, second page empty), each head diffed against its merge-base with `origin/main` at `f5cc78b63f3`:

```
packages/cli/test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts   held by: []
```

The only open claim under `packages/cli/test/` is #15611's `published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts`. Disjoint.

⚠️ A fact about the files open PRs touch, ⛔ not a clearance from CI's declared-claim gate.

### Why this one is worth a slot while the lane is serial-bound

This flake evicted PR #15506 from the merge queue on a shard its diff could not reach. A merge-queue eviction costs **every** lane a queue cycle, and under the one-re-run rule a second unlucky roll gets recorded as a real red. Fixing it pays out across seats, not just this one.

### ⛔ The one thing this card may not become

Skipping, quarantining, `.skip`-ing, or otherwise silencing the test is **not** an available repair — the card says so and this seat repeats it. The repair is in the harness's readiness/lifecycle handling: wait on the server's own ready signal, or retry the probe on `UND_ERR_SOCKET` a bounded number of times with the bound and its reason written down. A "flake" is not a root cause; `other side closed` with `bytesRead: 0` is a specific, diagnosable lifecycle race.

### Clause ②

Graded **NO**: a test-harness change, no `packages/spec/src/**` leg, no published payload touched. ⛔ Provisional — re-declared from the delivered diff.

## Back to `pm:queue` — the dispatch was lost to a container restart

The dispatch recorded above (`5548045697`) did not survive; this seat's container restarted and killed the implementing agent mid-flight.

**Nothing landed.** Measured from the refs, not assumed:

```
claude/issue-15545-serve-e2e-readiness-race   f5cc78b63f3415347d79375675b90c0763500c33
origin/main                                   f5cc78b63f3415347d79375675b90c0763500c33
```

Identical sha ⇒ zero commits, no PR, nothing partial to reconcile. Start clean; ignore that branch.

Label back to `pm:queue`, assignee cleared — `pm:dispatched` with nobody working is a false board. **The dispatch comment above stands in full** and is the brief for the next attempt, including the ⛔ line that this card may never become a skip or a quarantine.

⚠️ Worth noting for whoever takes it: the restart is itself a small demonstration of the card's own subject. Infrastructure interrupts work at arbitrary points, and a test that assumes its spawned server is ready when it is not is failing for a related reason — a process that isn't there yet, and a caller that assumed it was.

## Claim — implementing agent

Session `session_01D47qPfEWVPmhguWgBZCi5N`, dispatched by the `domain:cli` execution seat (#6024).

Branch: `claude/issue-15545-serve-e2e-readiness-race` (pushed empty at `d30ccb9bd96` = current `origin/main`, as the write-route probe; a prior dispatch on this card was killed by a container restart and landed nothing).

Declared file surface for this claim:

```
packages/cli/test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts
```

Any addition to that surface will be posted as an amendment on this thread before it is pushed.

⛔ Restating the binding fence so it is on the record from this side too: no `.skip`, no `.todo`, no quarantine, no retry-into-silence, no "bump the timeout and call it fixed". If I conclude the test cannot be made deterministic, I report that rather than stopping the measurement.

First measurement will be whether `other side closed` / `bytesRead: 0` is the harness racing its spawned `os serve`, or `os serve` itself closing the socket for a reason the test legitimately provoked — the second reading would move the defect into the product and is the one worth attacking.
